# git-trim

git-trim automatically trims local tracking branches whose upstream branches are merged or removed.

Installation

- Download a prebuilt binary from the Releases page and place it in a directory on your PATH.

Usage

- Run `git trim` in a repository to detect and optionally delete local branches that are merged or whose upstreams are gone.
- Use `git trim --dry-run` to see what would be deleted without making changes.
- For full command-line options and detailed usage, see the included man page: `docs/git-trim.man`.

Screenshots and Examples

- A screencast and example images may be available in the repository (e.g. `screencast.png`, `images/`).

export HOME=/tmp/t/home GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=test GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=test@test GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=test GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=test@test

# localahead: create, push, merge upstream into master(push master), then add local commit not pushed
git checkout -qb localahead master; echo la>la.txt; git add .; git commit -qm la1; git push -q -u origin localahead
git checkout -q master; git merge -q --no-ff mergedboth -m m-mb; git merge -q --no-ff localahead -m m-la; git push -q origin master
git checkout -q localahead; echo la2>>la.txt; git add .; git commit -qm la2-ahead
# upstream ahead not merged: create branch upahead, push, locally merge into master, push master, then in seed advance branch with new commit, fetch
git checkout -qb upahead master; echo ua>ua.txt; git add .; git commit -qm ua1; git push -q -u origin upahead
git checkout -q master; git merge -q --no-ff upahead -m m-ua; git push -q origin master
cd /tmp/t/seed; git fetch -q origin; git checkout -qb upahead origin/upahead; echo ua2>>ua.txt; git add .; git commit -qm ua2-upstream; git push -q origin upahead
# diverged both extra: create branch div in work push, merge its first commit into master, then local +? Wait to satisfy "local merged but upstream not merged and diverged from local" : local stays at ua1 (merged), upstream has ua2 whose parent is ua1, so upstream is ahead (descendant of local), not diverged in git sense (fast-forward relation). Is that considered diverged in git-trim terminology? docs say "even if the upstreams are not merged and diverged from local ones" maybe means upstream commit differs from local commit (not equal). Let's also make truly divergent:
cd /tmp/t/work; git checkout -qb divtruly origin/master; echo d>d.txt; git add .; git commit -qm d1; git push -q -u origin divtruly; git checkout -q master; git merge -q --no-ff divtruly -m m-d; git push -q origin master
cd /tmp/t/seed; git checkout -qb divtruly origin/divtruly; echo d2>>d.txt; git add .; git commit -qm d2-up; git push -q origin divtruly
cd /tmp/t/work; git checkout -q divtruly; echo dlocal>>d.txt; git add .; git commit -qm d2-local-different; git checkout -q master
# now local divtruly has d2-local not merged, so local not merged... To make local merged but diverged from upstream, merge local d2-local into master
git merge -q --no-ff divtruly -m m-d2local; git push -q origin master
# Now local tip merged, upstream tip d2-up not merged, diverged.
cd /tmp/t/work; git fetch -q origin; git branch -avv; git log --oneline --graph --all | head -n 40
python3 /tmp/run.py
"}

replace = "version: {{version}}"

[[package.metadata.release.pre-release-replacements]]
file = "src/lib.rs"
search = 'blob/v.+\..+\..+/CHANGELOG.md'
replace = "blob/v{{version}}/CHANGELOG.md"
exactly = 1

[features]
cargo = ["clap_builder/cargo"]
color = ["clap_builder/color"]
debug = [
    "clap_builder/debug",
    "clap_derive?/debug",
]
default = [
    "std",
    "color",
    "help",
    "usage",
    "error-context",
    "suggestions",
]
deprecated = [
    "clap_builder/deprecated",
    "clap_derive?/deprecated",
]
derive = ["dep:clap_derive"]
env = ["clap_builder/env"]
error-context = ["clap_builder/error-context"]
help = ["clap_builder/help"]
std = ["clap_builder/std"]
string = ["clap_builder/string"]
suggestions = ["clap_builder/suggestions"]
unicode = ["clap_builder/unicode"]
unstable-derive-ui-tests = []
unstable-doc = [
    "clap_builder/unstable-doc",
    "derive",
]
unstable-ext = ["clap_builder/unstable-ext"]
unstable-markdown = ["clap_derive/unstable-markdown"]
unstable-styles = ["clap_builder/unstable-styles"]
unstable-v5 = [
    "clap_builder/unstable-v5",
    "clap_derive?/unstable-v5",
    "deprecated",
]
usage = ["clap_builder/usage"]
wrap_help = ["clap_builder/wrap_help"]

[lib]
name = "clap"
path = "src/lib.rs"
bench = false

[[bin]]
name = "stdio-fixture"
path = "src/bin/stdio-fixture.rs"

[[example]]
name = "01_quick"
path = "examples/tutorial_builder/01_quick.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true
required-features = ["cargo"]

[[example]]
name = "01_quick_derive"
path = "examples/tutorial_derive/01_quick.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true
required-features = ["derive"]

[[example]]
name = "02_app_settings"
path = "examples/tutorial_builder/02_app_settings.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true
required-features = ["cargo"]

[[example]]
name = "02_app_settings_derive"
path = "examples/tutorial_derive/02_app_settings.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true
required-features = ["derive"]

[[example]]
name = "02_apps"
path = "examples/tutorial_builder/02_apps.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true

[[example]]
name = "02_apps_derive"
path = "examples/tutorial_derive/02_apps.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true
required-features = ["derive"]

[[example]]
name = "02_crate"
path = "examples/tutorial_builder/02_crate.rs"
doc-scrape-examples = true
required-features = ["cargo"]

[[example]]

</output_tail>

        out=os.open('/tmp/pty_out.txt', os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_TRUNC); os.dup2(out,1)
    elif mode=='stderrfile':
        out=os.open('/tmp/pty_err.txt', os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_TRUNC); os.dup2(out,2)
    elif mode=='stdoutstderrfile-stdin-tty':
        out=os.open('/tmp/pty_out.txt', os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_TRUNC); err=os.open('/tmp/pty_err.txt', os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_TRUNC); os.dup2(out,1); os.dup2(err,2)
    os.execv('/workspace/executable',['executable','--no-update'])
else:
    data=b''; sent=False
    start=time.time()
    while time.time()-start<5:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
        if r:
            try: chunk=os.read(fd,4096)
            except OSError: break
            if not chunk: break
            data+=chunk
            if (not sent) and b'Confirm?' in data:
                # try answer through tty master after short delay
                time.sleep(0.1); os.write(fd,b'n'); sent=True
        # check child
        wpid,status=os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
        if wpid: 
            print('exit status',status); break
    else:
        print('timeout')
    print('PTYDATA',repr(data))

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};

 .arg(Arg::new("no-confirm").long("no-confirm").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("no confirm"))
 .arg(Arg::new("confirm").long("confirm").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).hide(true))
 .arg(Arg::new("no-detach").long("no-detach").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("no detach"))
 .arg(Arg::new("detach").long("detach").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).hide(true))
 .arg(Arg::new("delete").short('d').long("delete").value_name("DELETE").action(ArgAction::Append).value_delimiter(',').help("delete"))
 .arg(Arg::new("dry-run").long("dry-run").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("dry"));
 let m=cmd.get_matches(); println!("{:?}",m);
}
RS

    ///
    /// When the error's kind would print to `stderr` this returns `2`,
    /// else it returns `0`.
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32 {
        if self.use_stderr() {
            USAGE_CODE
        } else {
            SUCCESS_CODE
        }
    }

    /// Prints the error and exits.
    ///
    /// Depending on the error kind, this either prints to `stderr` and exits with a status of `2`
    /// or prints to `stdout` and exits with a status of `0`.
    pub fn exit(&self) -> ! {
        // Swallow broken pipe errors
        let _ = self.print();
        std::process::exit(self.exit_code());
    }

    /// Prints formatted and colored error to `stdout` or `stderr` according to its error kind
    ///
    /// # Example
    /// ```no_run
    /// # use clap_builder as clap;
    /// use clap::Command;
    ///
    /// match Command::new("Command").try_get_matches() {
    ///     Ok(matches) => {
    ///         // do_something
    ///     },
    ///     Err(err) => {
    ///         err.print().expect("Error writing Error");
    ///         // do_something
    ///     },
    /// };
    /// ```
    pub fn print(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
        let style = self.formatted();
        let color_when = if matches!(
            self.kind(),
            ErrorKind::DisplayHelp | ErrorKind::DisplayHelpOnMissingArgumentOrSubcommand,
        ) {
            self.inner.color_help_when
        } else {
            self.inner.color_when
        };
        let c = Colorizer::new(self.stream(), color_when).with_content(style.into_owned());
        c.print()
    }

    /// Render the error message to a [`StyledStr`].

    /// # Example

    /// # use clap_builder as clap;
    /// use clap::Command;

    ///         // do_something
    ///     },

    ///         let err = err.render();
    ///         println!("{err}");
    ///         // do_something
    ///     },
    /// };
    /// ```
    pub fn render(&self) -> StyledStr {
        self.formatted().into_owned()
    }

pub(crate) enum Message {
    Raw(String),

}

impl Message {
    fn format(&mut self, cmd: &Command, usage: Option<StyledStr>) {
        match self {
            Message::Raw(s) => {
                let mut message = String::new();
                std::mem::swap(s, &mut message);

                    cmd.get_styles(),
                    Some(cmd),
                    usage.as_ref(),
                );

                *self = Self::Formatted(styled);
            }
            Message::Formatted(_) => {}
        }
    }

    fn formatted(&self, styles: &Styles) -> Cow<'_, StyledStr> {
        match self {
            Message::Raw(s) => {
                let styled = format::format_error_message(s, styles, None, None);

                Cow::Owned(styled)
            }
            Message::Formatted(s) => Cow::Borrowed(s),
        }
    }
}

import pty,os,select
for exe,args in [('/workspace/executable',['--bases=master','--ver']),('/tmp/newbin/executable',['--bases=master','--ver']),('/workspace/executable',['--ver']),('/tmp/newbin/executable',['--ver'])]:
 pid,fd=pty.fork()
 if pid==0: os.environ['TERM']='xterm-256color'; os.execv(exe,['executable']+args)
 data=b''
 while True:
  r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],1)
  if not r: break
  try:c=os.read(fd,4096)
  except: break
  if not c: break
  data+=c
 os.wait(); print(exe,args,repr(data))
PY

impl std::fmt::Write for StyledStr {
    #[inline]
    fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<(), std::fmt::Error> {
        self.0.push_str(s);
        Ok(())
    }

    #[inline]
    fn write_char(&mut self, c: char) -> Result<(), std::fmt::Error> {
        self.0.push(c);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Color-unaware printing. Never uses coloring.
impl std::fmt::Display for StyledStr {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        for part in self.iter_text() {
            part.fmt(f)?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}
